COUNTY OF SAN DIEGO BOARD OF SUPERVISORS - LAND USE
  REGULAR MEETING
  MEETING AGENDA
  WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 16, 2026, 9:00 AM
  COUNTY ADMINISTRATION CENTER
  BOARD CHAMBER, ROOM 310
  1600 PACIFIC HIGHWAY
  SAN DIEGO, CA 92101
County of San Diego Board of Supervisors
Land Use Legislative Session & Sanitation District
Wednesday, September 16, 2026, 9:00 a.m.

A.  Roll Call to Reconvene from Tuesday, September 15, 2026

B.  Closed Session Report

C.  Non-Agenda Public Comment
  Individuals can address the Board on topics within its jurisdiction that are not on the agenda.
  According to the Board’s Rules of Procedure, each person may speak at only one Non-Agenda
  Public Comment session per meeting. Speakers can choose to speak during either the General
  Legislative or Land Use Legislative Session.

D.  Approval of the Statement of Proceedings/Minutes
  Approval of the Statement of Proceedings/Minutes for the concurrent Special District meetings
  of the Sanitation District for June 24, 2026, and June 25, 2026.

E.  Consent Agenda
  All agenda items listed under this section are considered to be routine and will be acted upon
  with one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a member of the
  Board of Supervisors or the Chief Administrative Officer so requests, in which event, the item
  will be considered separately in its normal sequence.

Wednesday, September 16, 2026  1
 1.  Advertise and Award a Construction Contract for Drainage Culvert Repair and
  Replacement Associated with the Fiscal Year 2026-27 Resurfacing Program and Related
  California Environmental Quality Act Exemption (Districts: All)

  Recommendation by Chief Administrative Officer:
  1) Find in accordance with Section 15301(c) of the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) that the proposed project is categorically exempt from CEQA review because it
  consists of the maintenance of existing culverts involving negligible or no expansion of
  existing or former use.

  2)  Authorize the Director, Department of Purchasing and Contracting, to advertise and award a
  construction contract and to take any action authorized by Section 401 et seq. of the
  Administrative Code with respect to contracting for culvert repair and replacement.

  3) Designate the Director, Department of Public Works, as the County Officer responsible
  for administering the construction contracts in accordance with Board Policy F-41, Public
  Works Construction Projects.
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Approval Log
  Attachment A - Maintenance List

2.  General Services - Adopt a Resolution to Summarily Vacate Easements for Excavation,
  Embankment Slopes and Drainage in the Valley Center Community Plan Area and CEQA
  Findings (Vacation No. 2022-0046) (District: 5)

  Recommendation by Chief Administrative Officer:
  1) Find the proposed vacations are not subject to review under the California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to State CEQA Guidelines sections 15060(c)(2) and
  15060(c)(3) because the action would result in the summary vacation of excavation,
  embankment slopes, and drainage easements that are not needed for public purposes, and
  will not have a direct or reasonably foreseeable direct or indirect change in the
  environment and are therefore not a project as defined in CEQA Guidelines Section
  15378.

  2) Adopt a Resolution entitled: RESOLUTION TO SUMMARILY VACATE
  EASEMENTS FOR EXCAVATION, EMBANKMENT SLOPES AND DRAINAGE IN
  THE VALLEY CENTER COMMUNITY PLAN AREA AND CEQA EXEMPTION
  (VACATION NO. 2022-0046) (DISTRICT: 5) (Attachment C).

  3) Direct the Clerk of the Board to record the Resolution for Vacation No. 2022-0046

Wednesday, September 16, 2026  2
   pursuant to State of California Streets and Highways Code Section 8336.
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Approval Log
  Attachment A - Location Map
  Attachment B - Vacation Exhibit
  Attachment C- Resolution
  Attachment D - Exhibit A
  Attachment E - Exhibit B

3.  Adopt a Resolution to Apply for and Accept a State of California Strategic Growth
  Council Transformative Climate Communities Program Round 6 Implementation Grant
  and Related CEQA Exemption (Districts: 1 and 4)

  Recommendation by Chief Administrative Officer:
  1) Find that the proposed actions are exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15061(b)(3) of the California CEQA Guidelines.
  2) Adopt a Resolution entitled: Resolution Of The San Diego County Board Of Supervisors
  Authorizing The County Of San Diego To Apply For And Accept A State Of California
  Strategic Growth Council Transformative Climate Communities Program Round 6
  Implementation Grant.
  3) Authorize the Deputy Chief Administrative Officer for the Land Use & Environment
  Group, the Director of the Department of Public Works, and the Chief Sustainability
  Officer, or their designees, to apply for and accept a State of California Strategic Growth
  Council Transformative Climate Communities Program Round 6 Implementation Grant,
  and authority to execute all related documents if awarded including, but not limited to,
  applications, agreements, annual extensions, revisions, payment requests, and/or any
  agreements or memorandums of understanding with other entities as Co-Applicants,
  subgrantees, participants, and/or partners in the application and spending of grant funds
  received, that do not materially impact or alter the services or funding level and may be
  necessary for completion of the grant deliverables.
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Approval Log
  Attachment A - Resolution

4.  Set a Hearing for October 28, 2026:
  Ashwood Street Corridor Improvement Project and Right-of-Way Acquisition - Set a
  Public Hearing to Consider Adoption of a Resolution of Necessity and Related CEQA
  Findings (District: 2)

Wednesday, September 16, 2026  3
   Recommendation by Chief Administrative Officer:
  1) Find that the currently proposed action is not considered a project under CEQA Guidelines
  section §15378(b)(5). Today's action is limited to setting a public hearing for October 28,
  2026, at which time the Board of Supervisors will consider whether to adopt a Resolution of
  Necessity for acquisition of the subject parcels, and directing the Clerk of the Board to give
  the required notice. This action constitutes an organizational or administrative activity of
  government that does not approve, authorize, or commit the County to the acquisition of
  property, physical development, construction activities, or implementation of the underlying
  project, and therefore will not result in a direct or indirect physical change in the
  environment.

  2) Declare the Board’s intention to consider the adoption of a Resolution of Necessity to initiate
  an eminent domain action.

  3) Set a public hearing for October 28, 2026, to consider adoption of a Resolution of Necessity
  for the Ashwood Street Corridor Improvement Project for the following parcels: 2016-0281
  -A, -B (CARV), and 2016-0285-A,-B1,-B2,-C1,-C2,-D1,-D2,-E (Nelson).

  4) Direct the Clerk of the Board of Supervisors to send a "Notice of Hearing Regarding County
  of San Diego's Intention to Consider the Adoption of a Resolution of Necessity to Acquire
  Property By Eminent Domain" to each person whose name and address appears on the last
  equalized County assessment rolls for the following parcels 2016-0281-A, -B (CARV), 2016
  -0285-A,-B1,-B2,-C1,-C2,-D1,-D2,-E (Nelson).
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Approval Log
  Attachment A - Vicinity Map
  Attachment B - Property Map

F.  Discussion Items
  These items are presented for Board consideration and public discussion. Discussion Items may
  involve staff presentations and deliberation by the Board. The Board may provide direction,
  adopt recommendations, or take other appropriate actions. Please note that the Board may take
  items in a different order than they appear on the agenda.

5.  Approve the Starlight Solar Project to Allow for the Development of a Solar Energy
  Generation and Storage Facility and Certify the Environmental Impact Report (District:
  2)

  Recommendation by Planning Commission:
  On July 10, 2026, the Planning Commission considered the Starlight Solar Major Use Permit
  and made the following recommendations to the Board of Supervisors:

  1) Adopt the Environmental Findings, including certification and findings regarding the
  significant effects of the Project, the mitigation monitoring and reporting program, and the

Wednesday, September 16, 2026  4
   Statement of Overriding Considerations, and certify the EIR, Environmental Log PDS2022
  -ER-22-21-002, including consideration of the Staff-Recommended Project described below,
  pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) (Attachment A, on file with
  the Clerk of the Board).

  2) Adopt the Staff-Recommended Project described in this Board Letter, including the
  increased setbacks, and the Planning Commission's recommendations, including a water
  retention basin beneath the BESS locations to prevent contamination, locating the Phase II
  BESS as far south from the community as feasible, additional on-site dust monitoring,
  reallocation of community-benefit dollars from Phase II to Phase I, and additional
  community benefits towards the community of Boulevard.

  3) Approve Major Use Permit PDS2022-MUP-22-010 and impose the requirements and
  conditions set forth in the Form of Decision, including the revised community-benefit
  requirements, Phase II BESS siting, enhanced real-time dust-monitoring, BESS water
  retention containment requirements, and additional conditions to address community
  concerns (Attachment B, on file with the Clerk of the Board).

  4) Approve the Fire Protection and Mitigation Agreement between the County and Empire II,
  LLC (Applicant), and authorize the County Fire Warden or their representative to sign the
  agreement for the County (Attachment C).

  Recommendation by Department of Planning & Development Services:
  Planning & Development Services (PDS) concurs with the recommendations made by the
  Planning Commission, and makes the following additional recommendation to the Board of
  Supervisors (Board):

  1) Require Empire II, LLC (Applicant) to enter into a standard Defense and Indemnification
  Agreement in accordance with County Code Section 86.201 et seq. and authorize the Director of
  Planning & Development Services to execute the Agreement. If litigation is filed challenging the
  Board’s action on this Project, require the Applicant to provide security in the amount of
  $1,250,000 in the form of an irrevocable letter of credit or bond, in the form acceptable to
  County Counsel, within 10 days of litigation being filed (Attachment D, on file with the Clerk of
  the Board).

Wednesday, September 16, 2026  5
   Attachments: Board Letter - Strikeout
  Board Letter - Clean
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Approval Log
  Attachment A - CEQA Findings
  Attachment B - Form of Decision Strikeout
  Attachment B - Form of Decision Clean
  Attachment C - Agreement
  Attachment D - D-I Agreement
  Attachment E - Public Documentation
  Attachment F - Disclosure
  Attachment G - Action Sheet
  Attachment H - Hearing Report
  Attachment I - Planning Documentation

6.  Reopening the Agua Caliente Airport and Exploring Alternative Funding Options
  (Districts: 25)

  Recommendation by Supervisor Joel Anderson and Supervisor Jim Desmond
  1) Find that the proposed action is not a project subject to CEQA review pursuant to
  Section 15060(c)(2) of the CEQA Guidelines because the intent of the proposed action is
  to reestablish an existing airstrip and as a result will not result in a direct or reasonably
  foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment.

  2) Direct County of San Diego Airports to conduct the following actions and report back to
  the board within 60 days:
  a. Engage interested aviation stakeholders at each County operated airport including
  but not limited to: The Gillespie Field Development Council, The Gillespie Pilots
  Association, The Recreational Aviation Foundation, Aircraft Owners and Pilots
  Association, The Palomar Airport Advisory Committee, Fixed Base Operators,
  regarding the reopening of Agua Caliente airport and receive input, feedback,
  recommendations on runway rehabilitation, reconstruction, facilities
  improvements and general reopening of Agua Caliente Airport, and Airport
  Enterprise Fund expenditures;
  b. Establish necessary steps to bring Agua Caliente Airstrip back into the County
  Airports network and any operational impacts including, but not limited to
  resource needs for runway rehabilitation, reconstruction, ongoing maintenance,
  additional staffing requirements, and ongoing funding sources.

  3) While conducting the actions in Recommendation 2, direct the CAO to complete the

Wednesday, September 16, 2026  6
   following:
  a. Determine, prioritize, and finalize any necessary infrastructure improvements
  including but not limited to runway and parking surfaces, repairs, and other
  maintenance required by or related to existing Operating Agreements with State
  Parks, the California Department of Transportation, or other such entity or
  individual that may have ownership interest in the land on which the airstrip is
  located and identify associated costs including but not limited to runway
  improvements, ongoing general maintenance, utilizing potential one-time funding
  sources, Agua Caliente County Park Funds, Airport Enterprise Fund, or a
  combination thereof;
  b. Prepare all documents and processes for the completion of the reactivation,
  reinstatement, or establishment of a new Operating Permit with the California
  Department of Transportation, or such other State agency or agencies as may
  have authority over the permitting of airstrips;
  c. Research any current or potential future ownership, leasing, or other existing
  contractual arrangements with State Parks, or other such entity or individual that
  may have ownership interest in the land on which the airstrip is located, and the
  County of San Diego.
  Attachments: Board Letter- Strikeout
  Board Letter- Clean
  Agenda Information Sheet

G.  Special Districts
  When the Board of Supervisors meets as the governing body of a special district, they are acting
  in a different capacity than during their regular County business. In this role, the Board makes
  decisions that apply only to that specific district, such as approving its budgets, projects,
  policies, and operations. These actions are legally separate from the Board’s actions as the
  County of San Diego, and they apply only to the area and responsibilities of the special district.

  Special Districts Consent Agenda

7.  General Services - Sanitation District Sewer Easement Quitclaim in the Lakeside
  Community Plan Area and CEQA Findings (Vacation No. 2026-0031) (District: 2)

  Recommendation by Chief Administrative Officer:
  1) Find that the proposed action is not subject to review under California Environmental
  Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section 15060(c)(2) and (3) because
  it would only result in the quitclaiming of an unnecessary easement interest that is not
  needed for public purposes, and will not have a direct or reasonably foreseeable direct or
  indirect change in the environment and is therefore not a project as defined in CEQA
  Guidelines Section 15378.
  2) Find that the sewer easement is no longer required for District purposes.

Wednesday, September 16, 2026  7
   3) Approve and authorize the Director, Department of General Services, or a designee, to
  execute and record a quitclaim deed for the sewer easement described in Attachment B.
  Attachments: Board Letter
  Agenda Information Sheet
  Approval Log
  Attachment A - Map
  Attachment B - Exhibit

Special Districts Discussion Items

None

Wednesday, September 16, 2026  8
